The fixed source is selected #7000 event `["MOVE",415,3,99,false]`, index

coefficient index, spectator, numerical quantum and absolute phase. All
72 heads return; the original 43 guards persist; 29 new guards and all
70 private bodies are retired. No runtime host callback implements a gap.

## Complete cost and numerical domain

For old physical volume V_old and descriptor length E:

```
T <= 2^25 (f V_old + E + 1)
K_after <= K_entry + 2048 (V_old + E + 1).
```

Both codecs, all 18f address passes, all six factors, descriptors, staging,
source access, original-owner commit, guards and returns are included.
Erasure never refunds history. The unchanged graph retains direct
Theta(f V_old+E) cost; no accelerated nonleaf tariff is claimed.

prefix to be integral and fit the signed width. The selected complete-root
invariant **before** the right monomial implies this domain at unchanged
quantum 2^-(p+n), width p+h+2n+3. Its strict magnitude bound excludes
most-negative-word phase overflow; no extra 2^f input reserve is needed.

title: Construct orbit orderings with superpolynomial Gaussian tensor generator savings and explicit cost limits
body:
## What changed and why it matters

The preceding Gaussian tensor lower bounds fix lexicographic coordinate
order. This package constructs two arbitrary simultaneous row/column orders
with smaller ordinary Toeplitz generator bounds, and states the costs that
still prevent a runtime or unconditional-theorem claim.

The stronger family rotates disjoint blocks of distinct odd-prime lengths
p_i. For any repeated n-by-n factor B, n>=2, put T=n^d and P=product p_i.
The exact number of orbits is

`c=(T/P) product_i(1+(p_i-1)n^(1-p_i)) <= exp(8/9) T/P`.

Concatenating those orbits gives ordinary Stein rank and explicit ordinary
lower-times-upper Toeplitz generator count at most 2c, for both the forward
matrix and its inverse when it exists. Equality of factors within each block
suffices; arbitrary spectators are permitted. Common shifted factors, odd n
and nonsymmetric factors need no reversal symmetry or diagonal conversion.

For d>=8 choose k=floor(log2 d)-2 and Bertrand primes in (2^i,2^(i+1)). They
fit within d coordinates and have P>2^(k(k+1)/2). For identical Gaussian
factors the lexicographic minimum is 2T/n; the certified saving factor
P/(exp(8/9)n) grows faster than every fixed power of d for fixed n. This is
a representation saving, and the rank bound still grows with T.

The complementary even-n centrosymmetric construction uses complemented
rotation on ell power-of-two coordinates and gives the bound T/ell. Its
16-point binary example has exact forward/inverse rank 4 at q=1/2, versus
lexicographic rank 16. Either order may be preferable at a small parameter
point. Both proofs include explicit generators and inverse symmetry.

## Novelty and exact provenance

Canonical base: `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`. SOURCES.json
contains six exact canonical Git-blob/SHA256 pins. The proof restates its
algebra, and the verifier has no external runtime inputs.

This addresses the arbitrary-coordinate-order question left by the
[rank package at 326844a](https://github.com/CubeJerry/integer-mult-bounds/tree/326844a3e0c570fdafa4f3737095cd37154743a6/research/tensor-gaussian-displacement-rank)
and [rounding-margin package at 575491d](https://github.com/CubeJerry/integer-mult-bounds/tree/575491d5fc353eac26010e45e9ced60fc9870017/research/gaussian-generator-rounding-margin).
It changes the shift through a permutation; it does not contradict either
fixed-order theorem.

The complemented-rotation automorphism and binary orbit-length fact are
credited to Gregor, Merino and Mütze,
[*The Hamilton Compression of Highly Symmetric Graphs*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00026-023-00674-y),
section 3.3, equation (13), Lemma 3.4. They are not claimed new. The prime construction uses classical necklace
counting, coprime cyclic
products and Bertrand--Chebyshev prime existence, with primary credits to
[Moreau (1872)](https://www.numdam.org/item/NAM_1872_2_11__309_0/) and
[Erdős (1932)](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1932-01.pdf). The scoped contribution
is the explicit ordinary-generator consequence, exact two-family kernel
scope, verified prime-family growth and paid cost/precision boundary. Preserve the
originating source authors' credit, including Vlado Vojdanovski's
capped-phase-fusion work. No literature-wide priority claim is made.

## Why this matters

The preceding Gaussian orbit package constructs smaller ordinary Stein
generator representations, but leaves open how far the same global-symmetry
construction can go. A better cycle count alone also leaves its complete
cost unresolved. This package determines the optimal cycle-count scale over
**all exact permutation symmetries** of the stated homogeneous Gaussian
kernel, and proves that the specified dense boundary-vector format still
has almost quadratic size.

Canonical base: `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`.
Exact published predecessor:
[`8f1a09fb4f696bd5f20e1953210936308571416e`](https://github.com/CubeJerry/integer-mult-bounds/commit/8f1a09fb4f696bd5f20e1953210936308571416e).
Its proof objects were independently fetched and hashed in DEPENDENCIES.json;
the earlier branch is unchanged. This is an independent scoped theorem and
audit, not another conditional coefficient optimization.

## Exact results

For `H_xy=q^(||x-y||²) v^(sum(x-y))` on `{0,...,n-1}^d`, `n>=2`,
`0<q<1`, `v>0`, every exact symmetry is a coordinate permutation when
v!=1, or a signed coordinate permutation when v=1. This begins with
arbitrary permutations of all `T=n^d` vertices. The inverse has the same
group.

Writing g(d) for the classical maximum order in S_d, the minimum cycle
count c* satisfies `T/g(d)<=c*<4T/g(d)` for v!=1, and
`T/(2g(d))<=c*<4T/g(d)` for v=1. Disjoint prime-power rotations give the
upper bound, with a uniform correction at most `(3/2)exp(8/9)<4`. The
4-cycle exception is treated exactly. Landau's classical asymptotic then
determines the optimal logarithmic saving in this certificate class.

The corresponding dense2c-vector boundary format has optimum size
`Theta(T²/g(d))=T^(2-o(1))` for fixed n. Its writes alone eventually
exceed direct dense axis application, even with optimistic scalar costs.
The package charges a uniform selector, orbit enumeration and both layout
permutations rather than treating the new order as free.

Explicit entry/product separation conditions extend symmetry containment
to perturbed tables. A common rounding rule retains the construction, and
factorwise error epsilon transfers as
`delta<=d epsilon(1+epsilon)^(d-1)`. A polynomial-parameter/linear-precision
corollary preserves the same certificate scale even for tiny shifts.
Arbitrary errors can destroy symmetries, so an error bound alone does not
preserve the upper construction; coarse rounding can add symmetries.

the finite cycle count: lengths2+3 give12 cycles, while a5-cycle gives8.

claims by extrapolation.

Classify **every exact simultaneous permutation symmetry** of a normalized
heterogeneous Gaussian tensor on `product_i [n_i]`, with `n_i>=2` and positive
widths. The only symmetries are signed coordinate permutations preserving

has order at most two and at least `T/2` vertex cycles. If all shifts are
nonzero, the identity is the only symmetry. The proof also gives the exact
minimum cycle count and the same symmetry group for the inverse.

cycle format, not arbitrary displacement rank or other representations.

## Exact source and certificate boundary

At canonical main `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`, the retained

distinct odd source primes `s_i`, targets `t_i in {r,r/2}` and `rho_i=t_i/s_i`.

Write `m_i=(r/t_i)s_i`. These are distinct integers below r, including
across the two target-size groups by parity. Thus

`gamma_i^broad=b0*m_i/r`, with gaps at least `b0/r`,

`gamma_i^narrow=A*r/m_i`, with gaps greater than `A/r`.

The earlier format retains exactly `2cT` scalar slots, including prescribed
zeros. Hence `T²<=2cT<=2T²` for every exact symmetry here. Compression,

For `|a_i|<=1/2`, every ideal entry is at most one, so entry error eps

and

`2rho < min(exp(-2gamma_max)-exp(-4gamma_min), 2exp(-2gamma_max)*delta_gamma)`,

that each coordinate map is identity or reflection. No general graph
automorphism theorem or lower bound on tiny shifts is assumed.

The retained fine-prime gaps are at least `2^-o(p)`, so
`poly(p)2^(-Cp)` entry errors meet this guard eventually. Tiny shifts may
disappear and unequal errors may destroy reflections; the result is

ordering of an unshifted binary Gaussian tensor. For N=2^d and
H=⊗_i [[1,q_i],[q_i,1]], one proper real algebraic exceptional set suffices
so that every ordered forward matrix and every exact inverse has rank

`rank(A−ZAZᵀ) >= 2 ceil((N+3)/5)`.

Here Z is the ordinary nilpotent one-step shift. The good tuples are dense
and full-measure in `(0,1)^d`. This is a scoped universal theorem with exact
finite corroboration; **no new kappa** and no foundational-assumption discharge.

## What changes and why it matters

Earlier lexicographic rank results constrain the flattening order; earlier
orbit/symmetry results constrain the successor construction. This theorem
permits every simultaneous vertex order for the stated generic binary family.
It closes an arbitrary-order loophole for a linear rank floor without assuming
that the order follows a global symmetry.

The new proof uses XOR translation matchings. Their signed one-step
displacements consist of an even path and alternating cycles. Removing two
adjacent vertices per cycle leaves a principal minor with determinant ±1,
which is an isolated Gaussian polynomial coefficient. Two complementary
cycle counts imply the bound; a Schur-complement identity transfers it to
inverses. The coefficient proof works formally in every characteristic,
without claiming a good specialization exists over every finite field.

An exact sum of ordinary lower/upper triangular Toeplitz products needs at
